utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to tender the previous document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless it is objected to, it will be admitted as Exhibit P1088.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I might have cited the wrong number, and I apologise. What we should have on the screen is 01533.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, as we see on the first page of this document, the subject is: "A total of 400 persons who were driven from Bratunac to Pale." And they are listed on the subsequent pages, 18 pages. And if we could turn to the third page in English, and I believe it would be the same in B/C/S. Again, it indicates a total of 400 persons. The date is the 14th of May, 1992, and it is signed by Mr. Markovic, whose name we saw earlier in the decision to establish the Exchange Commission, as a member of the government's commission on behalf of the Serbian Ministry of the Interior for the exchange of prisoners of war, Slobodan Markovic. Now, Mr. Mandic, given the fact that the establishment of the commission was one of the very first things that the government did, is it your testimony that you don't -- you didn't know about these 400 people who were exchanged -- these 400 people from Bratunac who were exchanged via Pale on May 14th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never knew of this list or was I well versed in any way in respect of the exchange of these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is the same -- as far as you can tell, the same Slobodan Markovic who was a member of the commission; correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know who the man is. I don't know who Slobodan Markovic is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But you knew what the Exchange Commission was; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew this Colovic, Rajko Colovic, but I didn't know the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you knew that the commission was comprised of representatives from the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Interior, and the Ministry of Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. It was the prime minister who decided to establish the commission that way. I repeat once again, Mr. Tieger, Rajko Colovic was not an employee of the Ministry of Justice of the Serb Republic; never.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm not going to take you back to the previous passage of your testimony that I did, Mr. Mandic. Let me ask you: Were you -- isn't it the case that part of the impetus for the establishment of the commission was the number of people who were already incarcerated?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the motives were to establish this commission. Mr. Djeric can explain that to you, because he's the one who established it; that commission, that is. The commission was an independent governmental body that was answerable only to the government or, rather, to the prime minister. He could give you the best explanation for that; that is to say, to this honourable Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, we'll get into that in a moment. But, again, I'd like to know if the Justice Ministry or its predecessors, in the embodiment of you or other representatives, urged the Presidency to establish a central commission because of the increased influx of incarcerated persons.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the information we received came from the prime minister, Mr. Djeric, who was a member of this council and later on of the Supreme Command. The best-informed person in the government was the prime minister, among all the ministers. Everything we knew, we knew from him; we as members of the government, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This will be the last document of the day, Your Honour. If we could turn to 16249.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, I want to show you the report on the activities of the Ministry of Justice and Administration in the period May through October 1992.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And can we turn to the third paragraph of that report? It states: "Keeping in mind the demands for the successful establishment of the legal state and legal security of citizens, the ministry was forced to take a number of steps, primarily regarding the organisation of penal-correctional organisations, mainly the Butmir KP Dom Penal-Correctional Facility, considering the increased influx of incarcerated persons and the need for this penal organisation to be put to use. The ministry, therefore, urged the Presidency to establish a central commission for the exchange of prisoners of war, incarcerated and wounded persons, and dead bodies."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So again, Mr. Mandic, is it correct that the impetus or at least part of the impetus for the establishment of the Exchange Commission was the number of people who were incarcerated?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, only Djeric can give you an answer to that, Branko Djeric, the prime minister who established this commission before the Ministry of Justice was established. I cannot give answers in relation to something that happened before me, that is to say, before the Ministry of Justice was established. Call Mr. Djeric and let him explain it for you. He's the one who knows about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You said this was your report, Mr. Mandic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour. This was done by the professional services, and it was placed in context, as it were. You see that this is the Central Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of War that was established before the Ministry of Justice. So the Ministry of Justice could not initiate the establishment of the Central Commission when it was established before the ministry, itself, was established. So there's a mistake in this report. It probably has to do with the activities of the ministry and somebody from the ranks of the professionals wanted to make a contribution as if this were another thing that was done by the Ministry of Justice. But if you look back, you'll see that the commission was established on the 8th of May, and I was appointed on the 12th of May, and I was the first employee there. Now, was it someone from the old ministry, the joint ministry, that initiated that? I don't know. I mean, some from the ranks of the Serbian personnel, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mandic. Shall we leave the matter there, and we will resume on Monday morning, 9.00, on the 5th of July. I'm noting again the court scheduling in front of me, and I think it's possible to sit from 9.00 to 3.00. But otherwise, let me know before we begin on Monday morning. Have a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of July, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.03 p.m.,
